newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac Australia consumer index jumps in Nov.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac Australia consumer index jumps in Nov.

text.p: The Westpac/Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index for November rose 8.4 points or 8.3 percent to 109.8.

"After falling in the previous four months, consumer sentiment has rebounded strongly in response to good news on inflation and the Reserve Bank's decision to cut interest rates," said Bill Evans, Westpac's General Manager, Economics.
Evans said that this was the strongest immediate response to a rate cut recorded since March 1991.
"The authorities should be well pleased with their decision to ease monetary policy," he added.
The RBA cut official interest rates by 50 basis points last Wednesday to 6.50 percent.

The strong response to the policy easing was helped by the fact that the survey was conducted the weekend following the announcement and by the rapid action by banks to announce interest rate reductions for housing and business, Evans said.

He said the major factor in the rebound in consumer sentiment was a rise in confidence about economic prospects. Confidence about the economy over the next 12 months rose by 18 percent and there was now a net balance of respondents expecting good economic conditions.

"There was also a rise in the net balance who believe now is a good time to buy major household items. In the lead-up to Christmas this is encouraging news for the retail sector which has been experiencing lean times recently," Evans added.
